A session reading that list sees every other ordering rule stated and will meet `read`'s refusal as an unnamed one; the registered check only asserts that the skill names the Harness's paths and subcommands, so no mechanism catches the omission. One clause beside the `compare` one closes it — it harms nobody before then, and no round remains here to land it.

head: 673eb5ec6f4204ef9dd17cf1cd2a670e97f307f7
text: The registry `contract` for `license-assertion` (checks/registry.json:455) is still stale in the same file this diff edits, and this is the round-1 finding unanswered — only `case_floor` moved. It still describes the predicate as reading "a `push` whose changed paths are ALL under `policy/emissions/`" with no mention of the range or of the pooled union-over-commits predicate the owner selected, and its stated residue still reads that "the `git diff-tree` wiring that produces it is not [verified]" — a pipeline the job no longer runs, since the workflow now passes `--before`/`--after` and gathers nothing. The member's own header was updated to say the unasserted surface is now the two `${{ }}` expressions; the registry row, which is the surface a reader consults to learn what the member asserts, was not. The `efficacy_note` likewise still renders the clean state as "all 16 licence-predicate case(s) hold".

head: 673eb5ec6f4204ef9dd17cf1cd2a670e97f307f7
text: Acceptance 3's force-push shape is asserted in name but not in behaviour: the third unreadable-range branch — `git merge-base --is-ancestor` failing at `tools/assert-licensed.sh:159-161` — has no case. The case commented "A force push: `before` names a commit that is not in this repository at all" (checks/check-license-assertion.sh, `an unresolvable before falls to the same closed arm`) passes `6f6f6f...`, which fails at the earlier `git cat-file -e` guard and so exercises the same branch as no branch-specific fact of its own; on GitHub a force push delivers a `before` that *is* still an object in the repository — the old tip, present until GC — and is merely no longer an ancestor of `after`, so the arm a real force push takes is the one arm of the three that is unexercised. Cheap to close: a range case that commits, records the tip, then resets and commits differently, passing the recorded tip as `before`. Its `range_note` text also differs from the two that are covered, so the round-1 regrader would not catch a defect there either.

head: 673eb5ec6f4204ef9dd17cf1cd2a670e97f307f7
text: In range mode `tools/assert-licensed.sh` still silently overwrites `--message` (line 165 for a readable range, line 177 for an unreadable one), while the identical collision one line above — `--paths-file` alongside `--before`/`--after` — dies at line 150 with "two ways to supply the same fact; pass one". A hand invocation combining `--message` with a range is answered about a message it did not pass. Harmless in CI, where the job passes exactly one form; the asymmetry is the whole of it, and one more guard beside line 150 closes it.

head: 4547aea7d7c77fcb85a145e747a338054b649901
text: Round 1 findings 2 and 5 — the matcher read as a literal `|`-alternation — are repaired only in part. `covers()` now runs `re.fullmatch(matcher, t)`, so `.*` and `Bash.*` route and read `true`; that closes the regex-alternative arm. Two of the three shapes those findings named survive: `"matcher": "*"` raises `re.error` and is caught into `return False`, and an omitted or empty matcher — which Claude Code treats as matching every tool — gives `re.fullmatch("", "Bash")` → `None` → `False`. Both are registrations that DO route the member, printed as a false absence, which is the filed defect one level over. A one-line registry edit closes it: treat `*` and the empty/absent matcher as universal before the regex attempt. Non-gating — the entry reports and never gates, and today's literal `Bash|AskUserQuestion|...` registration reads `true`.

head: 4547aea7d7c77fcb85a145e747a338054b649901

If the line's carrier genuinely sits outside this repository per `specs/spec-external-deps/SPEC.md` §5, that statement belongs next to the audit in the note block.

head: 4547aea7d7c77fcb85a145e747a338054b649901
text: Round 1 finding 7 stands unchanged: the two conjuncts establish that the member is ROUTED TO, never that it EXISTS — nothing reads `~/.claude/hooks/lint-pr-merge.py`. A FAMILY row naming a member file absent from disk prints `true` while no `gh pr merge` is refused. The rewritten `capability` now names `~/.claude/hooks/lint-pr-merge.py` explicitly, so the gap between what the entry claims and what the read establishes widened slightly at this head; `answers` remains honest about it. A third `os.path.exists` conjunct closes it. A follow-up rather than an omission against #832, whose repair 1 licensed two conjuncts.

head: 4547aea7d7c77fcb85a145e747a338054b649901
text: The row match captures only the FAMILY tuple's third field, the declared tools; the fourth field — `"deny"` in `("lint-pr-merge.py", "PreToolUse", "Bash", "deny")` — is never read. A table edited to route the member with a non-deny action satisfies the whole read while `absence_signature`'s prohibition is no longer in force. Widening the row regex to capture and assert the action is a one-line change and would bind the property the entry's `capability` states.

head: 4547aea7d7c77fcb85a145e747a338054b649901
text: The regex repair is real but incomplete: `covers()` now uses `re.fullmatch(matcher, tool)`, which fixes `.*` and `Bash.*`, but two of the three shapes round 1 named still print a false absence. `"*"` — Claude Code's documented match-all matcher — is not a valid regex ("nothing to repeat"), and the `except re.error: return False` arm converts that raise into `false`; and an omitted or empty matcher gives `re.fullmatch("", "Bash") is None`, also `false`. Both are registrations that route the member. The `re.error` arm is right for a genuinely malformed matcher but wrong for `"*"`, which is not malformed in this domain — treating `"*"` and `""` as covering every declared tool before the regex attempt closes it. Non-gating: the entry reports and never gates, today's literal `Bash|AskUserQuestion|...` registration is what keeps it printing `true`, and the remedy is two lines in one registry string.

head: 4547aea7d7c77fcb85a145e747a338054b649901
text: Acceptance 3 is still discharged by claim on a surface that dies with the PR. The AC asks that the trust-environment line render the deny state "from the repaired read"; the PR body answers that the line reads `issue-sync hook-currency` and points at this run's own close. That may well be correct — `specs/spec-external-deps/SPEC.md` §5 puts that line's carrier outside this repository — but then the AC is *unbuildable here*, and that is a statement owed on a durable surface, exactly as the author reasoned when they moved Acceptance 2's audit out of the PR body and into the tracked registry note. One sentence in the same note block would make the two ACs consistent in where their evidence lives.

head: 4547aea7d7c77fcb85a145e747a338054b649901
text: The read still establishes that the member is ROUTED TO, never that it EXISTS: nothing opens `~/.claude/hooks/lint-pr-merge.py`. A FAMILY row naming a member file absent from disk prints `true` while no `gh pr merge` is refused — an absence signature suppressed over a control that is not in force, the mirror of the defect #832 was filed on. This head widens the exposure rather than narrowing it: `capability` now names `~/.claude/hooks/lint-pr-merge.py` explicitly as the thing asserted present, while `answers` is still honest that the question asked is only "is the deny routed to". A third `os.path.exists` conjunct closes it. Follow-up rather than an omission against the issue: #832's repair 1 licensed exactly two conjuncts.

head: 4547aea7d7c77fcb85a145e747a338054b649901
text: The FAMILY-row conjunct is a `re.search` over the dispatcher's raw TEXT, so a commented-out, docstring-quoted or otherwise inert `("lint-pr-merge.py", "PreToolUse", ...)` tuple satisfies it — the read asserts the row is *written* rather than *loaded*. Same class as the two conjuncts' proxy shape, one level smaller, and the cheap close is to import the dispatcher's table or to require the match to sit inside the `FAMILY` literal.

head: e7e5f322ea9830848fd11539f27ae0889474149d
text: The member's `contract` is reconciled in the large and still carries two clauses declaring assertions this act deleted. The kogaki#871 recovery paragraph — the one rewritten to say the input is COMPOSED from `RECONSTRUCTIBLE_FIELDS` "rather than rendered from a template file" — still ends its `Asserted:` list with "an absent template refuses rather than rendering prose with no instruction". There is no recovery template to be absent; the only absent-template refusals in the runtime are the cold reader's (`src/review-draft.mjs:845`) and the join template's (`:1818`), and both are already declared in their own paragraphs. And the kogaki#1016 paragraph still closes "the mechanical sibling `term-before-introduction` still answers on every Step either way" — that row left `src/review-items.json` with the hygiene items in this same act (`src/review-draft.mjs:5715` asserts it is gone, and the `case_floor_note` records case 4 being re-cut off it onto `grounds-unused`). Both are the shape round 1's finding 2 named, at two clauses rather than at whole paragraphs; the `removal_signal` reads against this contract, so a clause naming a deleted assertion is what a later removal act would try to preserve.

head: e7e5f322ea9830848fd11539f27ae0889474149d
text: The leak guard's comment block keeps its pre-repair paragraph in the present tense, one carrier over from the finding it just answered. "MATCHED AS A HEADING LINE, never as a substring" now describes an anchored substring search over JS source lines, not a heading-line match; and the reasoning that follows — "`/^#/`, ONE `#` AND NOT TWO", "`/^##/` … selects no line for it", "AND NOT `/^#{0,0}##/`, which fails BOTH ways: where awk supports intervals …" — is about an awk heading selector that no longer exists in the file, since the only awk left there slices the two renderer functions and the heading match is a `grep -qE`. The appended kogaki#1014 paragraph does bridge it, so a reader who reaches the end is not misled; a reader who diffs the comment against the code finds no `/^#/` to compare it with.

head: 4c2d77325417ec33ed9f69fa74e06d27f1cea723
text: The rewritten read swaps one carrier spelling for another rather than binding the property, which is the class #1020 promoted. `fam` is found by walking `tree.body` for `ast.Assign` nodes whose targets include the name `FAMILY`, so the row is read only when the dispatcher binds its table by a bare module-level assignment. An annotated binding — `FAMILY: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = (...)`, an `ast.AnnAssign`, which carries `target` and not `targets` — leaves `fam is None`, and the read prints `false` for a dispatcher that fully routes the member. Same for a table bound inside an `if`/`try` block at module level, or assembled by concatenation (the latter raising `ValueError` out of `ast.literal_eval` and typing COULD-NOT-ESTABLISH). Each of these is a false absence for a present control, one spelling further out — and the previous raw-text `re.search` would have found the row in the first two of them, so on those shapes this is a narrowing. The cheap close is to accept `ast.AnnAssign` alongside `ast.Assign` and to walk `ast.walk(tree)` rather than `tree.body`. Non-gating: the entry reports and never gates, today's dispatcher uses a bare assignment, and both the registered suite and `check-external-deps.sh` print the entry present at this head.

head: 4c2d77325417ec33ed9f69fa74e06d27f1cea723
text: A third match-all-adjacent spelling reaches `covers()` uncaught. `e.get("matcher", "")` collapses the absent and empty matchers, as the Review Focus states, but a registration written `"matcher": null` yields `None` — which is not in `("*", "")`, so it falls through to `re.fullmatch(None, t)` and raises `TypeError`, a class `except re.error` does not catch. The read then exits non-zero and is typed COULD-NOT-ESTABLISH against a settings file that is entirely readable and that does route the member, which is not what a completed read owes. One token closes it: `e.get("matcher") or ""`, which folds `null` into the empty-matcher arm the PR already treats as match-all.

head: 4c2d77325417ec33ed9f69fa74e06d27f1cea723
text: The suite cannot discriminate this change: it passes identically at the parent commit. `checks/check-external-deps.sh` runs an entry's `verification.command` against the live machine and is report-only by design ("NEVER FAILS ON THE WORLD"), and its fixture pass exercises `validate_entry` plus the state typing of synthetic `echo true` / `exit 127` commands — never the semantics of a registered entry's own read. So the nine-case mutation table in the PR body is the only evidence the `*` / empty-matcher / commented-out-FAMILY behaviours are what the entry now claims, and it is evidence that was produced and then discarded rather than codified. The next edit to this command re-opens the same class with nothing standing to catch it. The PR body already describes the apparatus that would close it — a sandboxed `HOME` carrying a synthetic `settings.json` and a copy of the dispatcher — so a fixture would be the run already performed, kept.

head: 4c2d77325417ec33ed9f69fa74e06d27f1cea723
text: The FAMILY resolution binds a spelling one further out than the one it just closed. `for node in tree.body` visits MODULE TOP LEVEL only and keeps the LAST matching `ast.Assign`, so a dispatcher that assigns `FAMILY` inside an `if`/`try` guard, builds it in a function, or seeds it as a literal and then extends it (`FAMILY += [...]`, `FAMILY.append(...)`) reads as `fam is None` or as a short table and prints `false` — a registration that DOES route the member, printed as an absence, which is exactly the defect class #1020 promoted. Same for `rows[0][2]`: it binds the tools to tuple position 2, so a FAMILY row that gains a field ahead of the tool string reads the wrong element and answers the matcher question against the wrong string, silently rather than by raising. Taking the last top-level assignment is otherwise the right choice — it is what Python would load — and today's dispatcher is presumably a plain top-level literal, which is why this prints `true`; the point is that the read is again true of the current shape rather than of the property.
